papers.title: Design and evaluation of an agent-based digital-twin-inspired simulation for metacognition research in higher education
papers.summary: Background There is a significant gap between sophisticated models of metacognition and empirical testing of these models in educational settings, especially the hierarchical AMERT model. Agent-based simulation frameworks, and their conceptual evolution toward simulation-based digital twins, remain largely underutilized in higher education as virtual laboratories for hypothesis generation, despite their potential to model complex developmental dynamics. Objective This study aimed to design and internally evaluate a simulation-based digital twin framework that combines the five-level AMERT model and agent-based architecture to investigate the dynamics of metacognitive development. Method Using Design and Development Research (DDR), we developed the framework through theoretical synthesis and subjected its conceptual content to expert review via a modified Delphi method with 12 experts. Student agents were simulated using NetLogo and represented four computational learner archetypes. Instructional scenarios were simulated for 150 ticks and repeated 50 times for each scenario, and internal consistency of the simulation logic was examined using Graph Neural Networks; the outputs remained systematically distinguishable across the predefined computational archetypes (89% classification accuracy). papers.title: Provenance-Gated Memory and Deontic Output Supervision for Epistemically Grounded Autonomous Agents
papers.summary: Autonomous agents driven by Large Language Models (LLMs) operating in extended multi-session settings suffer from two systemic failure modes: (1) recursive hallucination compounding, wherein unverified model-originated narration is committed to long-term memory and subsequently retrieved as established truth; and (2) fabricated action claims, wherein agents assert execution of irreversible real-world side effects without verified tool execution. We present the architecture and mechanical evaluation of Project Lucca, an open-source (GNU AGPLv3), local-first neuro-symbolic agent architecture designed for strict epistemic grounding. Lucca enforces two primary defenses: (1) a Six-Signer Cryptographic Provenance Gate that requires domain-separated HKDF HMAC-SHA256 signatures for persistent memory commits, enforcing an epistemic invariant at the database schema level that separates conversational continuity from factual grounding eligibility; and (2) a Deontic Truth-in-Receipt Output Supervisor that screens generated speech tokens against deterministic execution receipts before user presentation. We evaluate these mechanisms across an authored 73-test deterministic unit battery, a 100-probe live action-hallucination testbed across edge models (Gemma 4 E2B/E4B), and analyze documented production failure modes under compute constraints.

papers.title: From AI Disclosure to Human Handoff: Transparency, Trust, and Accountability in Automated Hospitality Services—A Structured Evidence Review
papers.summary: Automated hospitality services raise questions about transparency when guests first encounter artificial intelligence (AI) and when systems cannot resolve their requests. This structured evidence review examines AI disclosure, human escalation, trust, and organizational accountability. An access-limited synthesis mapped 19 empirical reports published between 2019 and July 2026, supplemented by relevant reviews and conceptual studies. Diverse methods, incomplete full-text access, and the absence of independent screening precluded meta-analysis and a comprehensive risk-of-bias assessment. The available evidence suggests that disclosure effects depend on service criticality and failure conditions, while recovery evaluations vary with problem severity, agent capabilities, and guest preferences. Responsibility assigned to a robot also differs from that attributed to its service organization. We develop a proposed executable transparency framework linking identity and capability information, accessible human assistance, information continuity, and clearly assigned recovery authority. Five propositions specify how these features could be examined in future research. The framework is conceptual and has not been tested as an integrated model. papers.title: Explainable Multidisciplinary Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Innovation and Intelligent Decision-Making Across Emerging Research Domains
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming scientific research, environmental sustainability, healthcare, and intelligent infrastructure. However, conventional AI approaches often lack interpretability, cross-domain adaptability, and transparent decision-making. This study proposes an explainable multidisciplinary AI framework integrating predictive analytics, explainable AI (XAI), and multi-criteria decision analysis to support sustainable innovation across diverse research domains. The proposed framework combines Random Forest, XGBoost, and Explainable Boosting Machines with SHAP-based feature attribution and multi-criteria decision analysis. A comparative evaluation design considers environmental sustainability, healthcare, and intelligent infrastructure as representative application domains. Models are assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), explanation fidelity, computational latency, and decision consistency. Baseline comparisons include conventional machine learning without explanations, explainable models without decision optimization, and the integrated framework. Sustainability indicators, interpretability, computational efficiency, and decision robustness are incorporated into a unified evaluation protocol. papers.title: Intelligent educational agent-based collaborative scaffolding for STEM interdisciplinary project-based learning: a multi-dimensional framework and empirical evaluation
papers.summary: STEM interdisciplinary project-based learning (PBL) asks students to knit together knowledge their courses have kept apart, and to do so while absorbing the ordinary friction of group work. Scaffolding designed for single-discipline tasks rarely keeps pace with either demand. This paper proposes an intelligent educational agent-based collaborative scaffolding model comprising four architectural layers—data perception, intelligent analysis, strategy decision, and interaction execution—supported by three specialized functional agents targeting cognitive guidance, process coordination, and reflection facilitation. A multi-dimensional feature fusion approach employing scaled dot-product attention diagnoses collaborative states in near real time, reaching a macro-averaged $$\:{F}_{1}$$ of 0.83 on a test set split by team, and a timing policy trained with Proximal Policy Optimization decides when to intervene while a fading rule decides when to withdraw. Twenty-four five-member teams (120 undergraduates) completed two interdisciplinary projects over six weeks under agent-based scaffolding, teacher-led scaffolding, or unsupported collaboration. Because students were nested in teams and several outcomes are defined at team level, condition effects were estimated with baseline-adjusted, cluster-robust models rather than treating the 120 students as independent. Design and Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence–Based Model for Predicting Twelfth-Grade Students’ Mathematics Performance Based on Individual, Educational, and Learning Technology Factors
papers.summary: Purpose: This study aimed to design and evaluate an artificial intelligence–based model for predicting the mathematics performance of twelfth-grade experimental sciences students based on individual, educational, and learning technology factors. Methods and Materials: This applied, quantitative, cross-sectional, and predictive study was conducted among twelfth-grade experimental sciences students in Isfahan, Iran. A total of 187 questionnaires were distributed, and after removing incomplete, inconsistent, and invalid records, data from 84 students were retained for analysis. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing individual factors, educational conditions, and learning technology variables, together with students’ recorded mathematics scores. The dataset was divided into training and testing subsets, and repeated five-fold cross-validation was used for internal model development. Multiple linear regression, ridge regression, lasso regression, elastic net regression, decision tree regression, random forest regression, gradient boosting regression, and support vector regression were compared. Model performance was evaluated using mean absolute error, root mean squared error, and the coefficient of determination. papers.title: Technology Research and Development and the Making of the EU’s Borders
papers.summary: Technology Research and Development and the Making of the EU’s Borders poses the question of how the Research and Development (R&D) of border security technologies constitutes a political practice of border security. It discusses how ideas of technology, borders and mobility control shape R&D at different stages, such as in formulating research calls or during research projects. In consequence, it is argued that through the prominent role of ideas and imaginations of security and control, R&D as a process reproduces these imaginaries and contributes to the maintenance of specific political orders. The book introduces the case of the EU’s Security Research Programme (SRP), which is funded within the large-scale Research Framework Programmes. Through the SRP, the EU funds projects specifically focusing on the EU’s border security system. Hence, it contributes to the functioning and maintenance of the EU’s border management infrastructures, such as information and surveillance systems. The involvement of different actors – security practitioners, policy administrators and researchers – at different levels makes the SRP a compelling case for understanding the political nature of border security R&D. This book therefore focuses on three levels – political relations and power structures of R&D, pertinent ideas and imaginations of security and work within projects – in order to achiev

papers.title: Uncertainty-aware offline reinforcement learning for LLM inference serving with heterogeneous SLOs
papers.summary: Abstract Large language model (LLM) inference workloads are bursty, have output lengths that are unknown at arrival, expose two resource-distinct phases (prefill and decode), and serve requests carrying heterogeneous service-level objectives (SLOs) on time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-per-output-token (TPOT). Prevailing schedulers rely on static heuristics that cannot adapt to this uncertainty, while online reinforcement learning (RL) is unsafe and sample-inefficient in production. We present URSA, an uncertainty-aware, risk-sensitive scheduler trained entirely offline , without interacting with a live serving system, on scheduling transitions generated by replaying historical request traces under existing heuristic schedulers. URSA (i) predicts a calibrated distribution over each request’s output length and derived key–value (KV) cache footprint rather than a point estimate; (ii) encodes the joint state of the waiting queue, heterogeneous GPU instances, and KV occupancy as a request–instance heterogeneous graph processed by a graph neural network; (iii) learns a dispatch policy with conservative, distributional offline RL whose reward jointly optimizes SLO attainment, goodput, and KV-overflow risk; and (iv) reserves memory at a class-dependent high quantile of the predicted footprint to bound out-of-memory events. papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Who benefits from LLMs? Prompt engineering competence and equity in higher education
papers.summary: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly becoming embedded in higher education, yet their benefits may be unevenly distributed. This study conceptualizes prompt engineering competence (PEC) as an equity-relevant interaction competence and examines whether differences in PEC are associated with perceived academic gains and perceived educational inequity. We adopt a two-stage quantitative design combining a cross-sectional survey with a within-subject prompt-quality experiment. Stage 1 reports a survey of Chinese undergraduates who have used LLMs ( N = 380), measuring PEC, perceived academic performance gains, perceived educational inequity, family digital capital, gaming experience, and a planning/independent-work tendency. Regression and mediation analyses show that PEC was strongly associated with perceived academic gains, while its association with perceived inequity was statistically significant but small. Background resources and learning-related experiences and dispositions explained substantial variance in PEC, especially gaming experience and planning/independent-work tendency, and the association between family digital capital and perceived academic gains was largely indirect through PEC. Stage 2 conducts a within-subject prompt-quality experiment across four higher-education task types and four popular models, comparing basic prompts with a student-oriented fi

papers.title: A Rapid Systematic Review of AI‐Generated and Human‐Generated Real‐Time Feedback in Nursing Education
papers.summary: AIM: To explore the effects of AI-generated and human-generated real-time feedback on learning outcomes and experiences among undergraduate nursing students. BACKGROUND: Timely, high-quality feedback is crucial in nursing education to support clinical reasoning, skill development, and student engagement. While human-generated feedback remains central to pedagogy, emerging AI offers real-time feedback that complements traditional approaches. Understanding how both interventions influence student learning is critical to informing future curriculum and clinical practice. METHODS: We conducted a rapid systematic review of quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies across major databases from 2018 to 2025. Eligible studies involved undergraduate nursing students receiving real-time feedback generated from AI or humans. The Sample, Phenomenon of Interest, Design, Evaluation, and Research Type framework guided inclusion, and the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool assessed methodological quality. FINDINGS: Nine studies were included. AI-generated tools supported timely, consistent, and individualised learning, contributing to student engagement, confidence, and skill development. Educator-mediated feedback, including technology-assisted and conventional human feedback approaches, supported student satisfaction, reflection, and emotional support. papers.title: Explainable AI for Intelligent and Sustainable Decision-Making
papers.summary: Organizations increasingly use artificial intelligence (AI) to improve strategic planning, operational efficiency, and sustainability. However, conventional machine learning models often lack transparency, limiting managerial trust, accountability, and the practical adoption of AI-driven decisions. This study proposes an explainable AI (XAI) framework that integrates predictive analytics, interpretable machine learning, and sustainability indicators to support transparent, reliable, and evidence-based decision-making across technological, organizational, and environmental dimensions. The proposed framework combines Random Forest, XGBoost, and Explainable Boosting Machines with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME). Evaluation uses a benchmark dataset containing operational performance, resource consumption, organizational efficiency, and environmental indicators. Comparative experiments assess predictive accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), explanation consistency, decision latency, computational cost, and sustainability performance. Baseline models include Logistic Regression, conventional Random Forest, and XGBoost without explanation mechanisms. Ablation studies examine the individual contributions of interpretability and sustainability-aware optimization

papers.title: Exploring the potential of hybridized metaheuristic algorithms for photovoltaic model parameter estimation
papers.summary: Abstract Proper modeling of photovoltaic (PV) cells is a highly non-linear and multidimensional problem whose optimization using standalone meta-heuristic techniques faces premature convergence due to the large number of parameters. This paper seeks to fill in a major gap in the literature through a permutation study of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Differential Evolution (DE), Simulated Annealing (SA) and Nelder-Mead (NM) simplex method to determine the optimal "hand-off" scheme for balancing exploration and exploitation. The proposed approach has been evaluated using SDM, DDM, and TDM using R.T.C. France silicon cell, Photowatt-PWP 201 module and an independent set of data on flexible dual junction amorphous silicon cell. To ensure state-of-the-art robustness of the hybrid approach, it was also benchmarked against CEC 2017 test suite. Statistical analysis from 30 runs has been performed using Wilcoxon signed-rank test ( $$p<1.86\times {10}^{-9}$$ ), demonstrate that a sequential "Global-to-Local" transition (PSO–NM) achieves superior precision and stability, yielding a mean RMSE of $$9.32 \times 10^{ - 4}$$ for the SDM and $$1.16 \times 10^{ - 3}$$ A for the 9-parameter TDM, with coefficients of determination ( $${R}^{2}$$ ) exceeding 0.9999. Complexity analysis via the Number of Function Evaluations (NFE) shows that this hybrid method is computationally worth the effort

papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: Designing a Curriculum Model Based on Artificial Intelligence and Purposeful Physical Activity to Enhance Learning Self-Regulation, Mental Health, and Psychological Well-Being among Students
papers.summary: Objective: The objective of this study was to design and validate a curriculum model based on artificial intelligence and purposeful physical activity with emphasis on enhancing learning self-regulation, mental health, and psychological well-being among students. Methods and Materials: This applied developmental study was conducted using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. In the qualitative phase, 20 experts in curriculum studies, educational technology, artificial intelligence in education, physical education, educational psychology, and student mental health were selected through purposive criterion-based sampling from Tehran and participated in semi-structured interviews. The interview data were analyzed using thematic analysis to extract the main dimensions, components, and indicators of the proposed curriculum model. In the quantitative phase, 384 secondary school students from Tehran were selected through multistage cluster sampling during the 2025–2026 academic year. Data were collected using a researcher-made curriculum model validation questionnaire, a learning self-regulation questionnaire, the General Health Questionnaire, and a psychological well-being scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling. Findings: The inferential findings showed that the final curri

papers.title: Learning control policies from heterogeneous multi-horizon time series in battery energy management systems
papers.summary: This paper introduces Representation-to-Decision (R2D), an end-to-end imitation learning framework that maps heterogeneous multi-horizon time-series inputs directly to battery control decisions through modular Temporal Feature Extractors (TFEs) and a shared latent representation, without an explicit load and PV forecasting step. While accurate forecasting improves prediction quality, optimal control performance remains unguaranteed in prediction-then-optimization pipelines; standard Reinforcement Learning (RL) lacks the long-horizon temporal awareness due to short-window observations, even when forecast signals are available as additional inputs. R2D offers a different perspective: rather than forecasting first and deciding second, it learns to decide directly from raw temporal inputs, with control optimality anchored by an aging-aware Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) expert through Behavior Cloning (BC). Benchmarked against six controllers on a high-fidelity electro-thermal battery simulation across five industrial sites, R2D achieves 62--77\% of the global clairvoyant optimum, outperforms the tested Model Predictive Control (MPC) and RL benchmarks, and yields battery degradation nearly identical to its MILP teacher across all five sites. Comprehensive ablation studies over temporal backbone, model size, expert formulation, aging-cost weighting, and horizon configuratio

papers.title: Quality versus quantity: including imperfect training data improves prediction of user satisfaction in software projects
papers.summary: This study explored the impact of data quality and quantity on predicting user satisfaction in software projects using the ISBSG dataset. This study evaluated the performance of machine learning models by varying the data variants, i.e. strategies for including low-quality data in the training subsets. A rigorous methodology was employed to ensure the reliability of the results and validate the conclusions. It involved repeated nested cross-validation, standardised accuracy, win–tie–loss analysis, matched-pairs rank biserial correlation, Scott–Knott effect size difference test, and Kendall’s W. The findings suggest that models predicting user satisfaction trained on larger datasets, despite containing low-quality data, usually outperformed those trained on smaller, high-quality datasets. Hence, expanding the training data can improve predictive accuracy, even if it comes at the cost of data quality. Support vector machines (SVM) and extreme gradient boosting trees delivered the most accurate predictions across all data variants. A combination of SVM with the data variant involving all cases and attributes, where at least 40% of values were valid (non-missing), was the most accurate. Obtained findings enabled the formulation of a preliminary recommendation: when working with ISBSG or similar datasets, researchers and practitioners prioritising predictive accuracy of user satisfa

papers.title: Olanzapine induces Mdivi-1-resistant disruption of insulin signaling in skeletal muscle cells
papers.summary: Introduction Second‐generation antipsychotics such as olanzapine (OLZ) are widely prescribed because they produce fewer extrapyramidal adverse effects than first‐generation agents. However, OLZ is strongly associated with metabolic dysfunction, and alterations in mitochondrial dynamics have been proposed to contribute to these effects. We investigated whether OLZ‐induced mitochondrial dysfunction is linked to impaired insulin signaling in skeletal muscle cells and explored a potential interaction with the mitochondrial fission regulator dynamin‐related protein 1 (DRP1). Methods L6 skeletal myoblasts were treated with OLZ, alone or in combination with the mitochondrial fission inhibitor Mdivi‐1. Insulin signaling, glucose uptake, mitochondrial morphology, and insulin‐stimulated mitochondrial bioenergetics were evaluated. In parallel, molecular dynamics simulations and MM/PBSA calculations were performed using a common DRP1/Mg 2 + receptor model to compare the interactions of protonated OLZ and Mdivi‐1 within the DRP1 GTPase domain. Results OLZ reduced insulin‐mediated signaling and glucose uptake, promoted mitochondrial fragmentation, and impaired the insulin‐induced increase in mitochondrial bioenergetic activity. papers.title: How to overcome the productivity pains of digital transformation? The U‑shaped TFP trajectory of Chinese agricultural firms, fixed‑asset constraints and subsidy threshold effects
papers.summary: Digital transformation has profoundly reshaped agricultural production systems, yet its productivity effects remain insufficiently explored. Using panel data of Chinese listed agricultural firms from 2010 to 2022, this paper examines the effects, mechanisms, moderation, and heterogeneity of digital transformation on total factor productivity (TFP). First, digital transformation exerts a significant U-shaped nonlinear effect on TFP: the linear coefficient is −0.154 ( p < 0.01), and the squared coefficient is 0.036 ( p < 0.01), indicating that early-stage fixed asset accumulation, organizational restructuring, and system adaptation frictions drag down TFP, while after crossing the critical threshold, network synergy and factor allocation optimization drive sustained TFP growth. Second, the fixed asset-to-revenue ratio serves as a key transmission channel, forming a nonlinear mediation path of “digitalization → fixed asset-to-sales ratio → TFP.” Bootstrap tests show that the indirect effect turns from negative to positive as digitalization increases and is significant only at high levels. Third, government subsidies significantly moderate the U-shaped relationship, shifting the turning point leftward and increasing curvature, reflecting a “turning point forward shift and dividend amplification” mechanism. papers.title: Improved regressive maintenance in smart Industry 4.0 using embedded systems with machine learning techniques
papers.summary: Despite extensive research in this field, fourth generation of industrial revolution or the "Industry 4.0," remains rarely used. This technology enables sectors to make intelligent on taking decision, knowledge, problem-rectifying, self-diagnosis, configuration, and automation feasible. This research study proposes to transform the food sector into a smart Industry 4.0 by utilizing sensor and machine learning (ML) methods. The motive of this article is to use a variety of sensor data, such as motor temperature, oven temperature, gear pump temperature, vibration, current consumption, and motor speed, to forecast the likelihood of machine failure in the food processing business. We create models using artificial neural networks (ANN) and linear regression with the data collected from these sensors to estimate the likelihood of failure. The findings demonstrate that both of the generated models have excellent accuracy in forecasting the chance of failure. The technology could help the food sector transition to sector 4.0, where networked equipment exchanges data to maximize production efficiency. In summary, the present study showcases the potential of sensor-based analysis maintenance methods in the food sector and emphasizes the need to incorporate Industry 4.0 principles to enhance the effectiveness of food processing facilities.

papers.title: Modality aware feature taxonomy for robust AI driven intrusion detection across heterogeneous cyber physical data
papers.summary: We investigate whether conditioning heterogeneous security metadata by semantic type—rather than applying uniform normalization—improves intrusion detection performance by up to 22.9 percentage points. To operationalize this hypothesis, we propose the Modality-Aware Feature Taxonomy (MAFT), a preprocessing framework that classifies IDS features into six semantic groups (temporal, volumetric, behavioral, identity, protocol-specific, and statistical) and applies group-appropriate normalization: robust scaling with outlier clipping for heavy-tailed volumetric features, z-score standardization for temporal measurements, and bounded scaling for categorical and identity fields. MAFT’s contribution is methodological rather than algorithmic: it formalizes IDS preprocessing as a feature-modality conditioning problem, provides a transparent taxonomy-to-scaler mapping for security metadata, and characterizes when such conditioning is likely to matter. We evaluate MAFT through a four-stage progressive ablation across six public IDS benchmark datasets spanning enterprise network traffic (UNSW-NB15, CICIDS2017), IoT environments (ToN-IoT, N-BaIoT, Edge-IIoTset), and industrial control systems (HAI), comprising 24 centralized experiments with multi-seed statistical validation for UNSW-NB15 multiclass and binary classification for all six datasets. papers.title: AI-Assisted Feedback and Perceived Academic Performance: The Mediating Roles of Digital Motivation and Self-Regulated Learning Among Indonesian University Students
papers.summary: The increasing use of artificial intelligence in digital learning presents new opportunities to improve the quality of academic feedback, although its educational value may be associated with students’ motivational and self-regulatory characteristics. This study examined the relationships among AI-assisted feedback, digital motivation, self-regulated learning, and perceived academic performance of university students. Survey data were obtained from 337 students at two private universities in Makassar, Indonesia. The measurement model was evaluated through confirmatory factor analysis in LISREL 8.7 using the full eligible sample, whereas the structural model and mediation pathways were tested in AMOS 24 using 290 cases after multivariate outlier screening. The qualitative phase involved semi-structured interviews with 15 purposively selected students to explain and contextualise the quantitative findings. The interview data were analysed using a theory-informed thematic analysis. Results showed that perceived AI-assisted feedback was positively associated with digital motivation and self-regulated learning. Digital motivation was positively associated with self-regulated learning, while both digital motivation and self-regulated learning were positively associated with perceived academic performance. papers.title: ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, DESIGN, AND CHANGE
papers.summary: Organizational structure determines how work, authority, information, accountability, and interdependence are arranged; organizational design determines whether those arrangements remain appropriate as enterprise commitments and conditions change. This chapter develops a critical, integrative treatment of structure and organizational change across firms, cooperatives, public institutions, and digitally mediated networks. It compares contingency theory, information-processing approaches, sociotechnical systems, organizational ecology, institutional theory, and organizational ambidexterity, identifying their explanatory mechanisms, competing predictions, and empirical limitations. The analysis develops twelve connected domains, from specialization, structural configurations, coordination, culture, and growth to diagnostic methods, change programmes, distributed work, innovation, and design justice. A transparent secondary-source synthesis draws on original scholarship, Rwanda's Integrated Business Enterprise Survey 2024, East African Community institutional arrangements, and peer-reviewed international hybrid-work evidence. Original decision-support instruments include a structure-selection decision tree, a structural trade-off matrix, a cross-functional workflow diagnostic, a governance and escalation design, and reproducible redesign economics. papers.title: PRINCIPLES, THEORIES, AND FUNCTIONS OF MANAGEMENT
papers.summary: Management is the practice of coordinating collective action when purposes are plural, knowledge is dispersed, resources are constrained, and outcomes remain uncertain. This chapter develops an integrated and critical account of managerial work, its intellectual traditions, and its recurrent functions of planning, organizing, leading, and controlling. Rather than treating the classical management cycle as a deterministic sequence, it interprets these functions as interdependent, revisable processes mediated by authority, judgment, organizational context, and accountability. Scientific, administrative, bureaucratic, human-relations, systems, contingency, behavioral, institutional, and contemporary evidence-based perspectives are assessed for their mechanisms and limitations. A transparent, purposive synthesis of published scholarship and authoritative secondary evidence anchors the account in Rwandan enterprise conditions, with comparative insight from an international manufacturer and experimental studies of management improvement. The chapter provides a management-cycle diagram, a responsibility-assignment matrix, a decision log, a management KPI tree, worked calculations, a resource-allocation scenario, and evaluative instruments. papers.title: BUSINESS OWNERSHIP, INSTITUTIONS, AND REGULATION
papers.summary: An enterprise acquires legal and economic capacities through institutions that determine who may own assets, transact, appoint decision makers, use information, enter markets and answer for harm. This chapter examines business ownership, corporate personality, contracting, intellectual assets and regulatory obligations as interacting elements of enterprise design rather than isolated legal formalities. It brings institutional economics, property-rights theory, agency and stakeholder accounts, comparative corporate law and responsive regulation into critical dialogue. A targeted documentary synthesis combines foundational scholarship with officially published Rwandan laws and institutional guidance current to 24 October 2026, including the 2024 cooperative and intellectual-property enactments and Rwanda's 2026 competition and consumer protection law, with its specific e-commerce provisions. The analysis distinguishes statutory rules, institutional guidance, comparative frameworks and illustrative choices; it does not substitute for jurisdiction-specific legal advice. An original formation decision framework, legal-form matrix, legal-obligations register and compliance calendar translate legal complexity into managerial decisions. papers.title: AI-Driven Data Supply Chain
papers.summary: This book explores the transformation of data management through AI-driven solutions, emphasizing the critical role of an intelligent and adaptive data supply chain. It covers essential topics such as AI-powered data discovery, automated data pipelines, data governance, and real-time analytics. The book also examines practical applications, including cost optimization in cloud environments, security and privacy considerations, and real-world case studies. Key features: Defines a new data foundation based on the concept of a data supply chain and bridges the gap between theory and implementation through AI-driven approaches. Promotes the development of a comprehensive Data and AI ecosystem. Presents a focused blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, supported by hands-on examples and step-by-step frameworks. Focuses on AI-powered data lifecycle management, with automation and visibility at its core. Applies the shift-left principle by embedding Generative AI into data foundation practices, proposing and implementing innovative and improved methodologies. This book is intended for data professionals, AI practitioners, IT managers, business analysts, senior executives, product managers, and academics specializing in data science and supply chain management.

papers.title: ARC: Open Infrastructure Towards Assessable Regulation Compliance Checking
papers.summary: Automated compliance checking tools often reports a final pass or fail result, providing limited traceability. This paper presents Assessable Regulatory Compliance (ARC), an open-source engine that produces structured compliance evidence alongside approval decisions. ARC combines a rule-execution pipeline, a six-status result model, per-check classification of rule-element pairs, routed coverage gaps, and evidence records. The engine is independent of authoring tools and information model schema. ARC was evaluated on a sample house and a real high-rise apartment model using an Industry Foundation Class (IFC) adapter. Results show that it distinguishes measured compliance outcomes from missing information, non-applicable rules, limited geometry, and cases requiring reviewer judgment. A lobby-width example demonstrates how one requirement can yield PASS, HUMAN_REQUIRED, or INCONCLUSIVE statuses depending on geometry and model tagging. ARC provides a foundation for open, auditable, and modular compliance evidence in digital building permit workflows.

papers.title: Q&A or Document-Based? The Effects of Interface Type on How Screen Reader Users Access Interconnected Documents
papers.summary: Blind and low-vision (BLV) users are increasingly engaging with large language model (LLM) interfaces to access documents, but it is unclear how such systems support or hinder their ability to build interconnected knowledge. To examine this gap, we compared a Question–Answer Interface (QAI) that supports open-ended conversational inquiry, with a Document Interface (DI) based mostly on traditional structured text document navigation. We recruited 16 BLV screen reader users where they used both interfaces to explore two fictional worlds. Data from interaction logs, concept maps, decision-based tasks, and semi-structured interviews provide comparative insights into how interface design supports knowledge construction. Findings show that participants visited more distinct documents with the DI and formed larger and more correct mental models with the DI than with the QAI. They were also more able to apply the knowledge they had gained. Simultaneously, many still preferred the QAI and often estimated that they had explored more, formed better mental models and applied their models better when acquiring the information with the QAI, despite this not being the case. Our analysis suggests possible interface design reasons for these differences and highlights some of the risks introduced by using question-answer interfaces to access information spaces.
